001: It's my first week and I still find it hard to keep up with the pace of the meetings.
Don't worry, it's completely normal. At first we all feel that way.
Did you also have to adapt to this way of working?
Of course we did. Here we really value direct communication and initiative.
So, do you think I should share my opinions more in the meetings?
Exactly, but always with respect and waiting for your turn to speak.
002: I've noticed that people here don't usually eat lunch at their desks.
That's right. We prefer to take a break and eat together in the cafeteria.
And does that help create a better atmosphere among coworkers?
A lot. It's the perfect time to get to know each other outside of work.
I think it's a great custom, honestly.
Well, go for it and join us tomorrow. I'll introduce you to more people.
003: Could you explain to me how the expense approval system works?
With pleasure. First you have to register the request on the internal platform.
I see, and then, who is in charge of reviewing it?
The head of your department reviews it, and then it goes to finance.
Okay, it seems like a pretty clear process.
Yes, but if you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask me.
004: I was surprised that the boss didn't get angry about yesterday's mistake.
Here we prefer to analyze failures calmly and look for solutions.
And there aren't usually any scoldings or shouting in this team?
No, not at all. That style doesn't fit with our company culture.
Honestly, it's really nice to work in such a healthy environment.
Definitely, and that way we all learn much faster.
005: I've seen that many coworkers work from home on Fridays.
Yes, we have a fairly flexible remote work system.
And how do they decide which days they can stay home?
Normally they agree on it with their team and as long as there are no meetings.
I think it's a very modern and sensible policy.
I like it too, because it helps balance your personal life.
006: Do you recommend any course for me to learn more about project management?
I suggest the internal workshop they organize on Thursday afternoons.
And is it aimed at new people or also at veteran employees?
It's for all levels, so you can definitely take advantage of it.
Great, then I'll sign up as soon as I can.
Do it, because the spots fill up very quickly.
007: I'm not used to being praised so much for a job well done.
Well, here we do it often, because we value daily effort.
And is teamwork also recognized, or only individual work?
Both, although the team always carries a lot of weight.
I'm glad to hear that, because I like collaborating with others.
And it shows, your coworkers already speak very highly of you.
008: I feel a bit embarrassed to ask my coworkers for help so soon.
You shouldn't. Here asking for help is a sign of responsibility.
Do they really not see it as a lack of ability?
Not at all. We prefer that you ask rather than make avoidable mistakes.
That really puts my mind at ease, honestly.
I'm glad. Remember that we've all been through the same thing.
009: I've noticed that meetings always start with a review of the objectives.
Yes, that way we make sure we all have a clear direction.
And are they usually that short, or do some go on too long?
We try to keep them agile, but sometimes complex topics get in the way.
I understand, in the end the important thing is that everyone leaves with clear ideas.
Exactly, that's the key to our team.
010: What do you think of the company dinner they organize every quarter?
I think it's a fantastic initiative for strengthening bonds.
And do a lot of people usually attend, or only the more veteran ones?
You'd be surprised, almost the whole team signs up for these celebrations.
Then I won't think twice and I'll sign up for the next one.
Very good, that way we can get to know you better outside of the work environment.
